Cuttings dropping in the hole? It's the fluid, not the pump.
When the cuttings can't ride the fluid out, they settle. Pack the annulus. Grab the rods.

Carry Flow is built to hold those cuttings in suspension. Pump's running, they move. Pump stops, they stay put instead of dropping back down the bore.

That's the difference between a clean trip out and a stuck string.

Most jobs, most ground, Carry Flow earns its keep. The trick is matching the dose to what the hole is throwing at you.
Tougher ground than usual? Give the team a call and we'll dial in the program.

Carry Flow does more work than most crews give it credit for.
Long bores. Coarse cuttings. Slow returns. That's where Carry Flow earns its money.

Hole's clean, cuttings come out, the pump isn't fighting a packed annulus. Crew gets through the shift without a stuck string story.

Pair it with Filter Low when the wall won't seal and you've got a fluid program that holds up across most ground in AU and NZ.

Short clean bores in tight sand? You can run lighter. The point is matching the fluid to the job, not the job to the fluid.
Planning a bore that's worrying you? Phone the team. We'll build the program around the ground.
